text: Air Sealing, Attic Floor Insulation, and Duct Sealing Accessing Results This documentation covers the “advanced air sealing, attic floor insulation, and duct sealing” measure upgrade methodology and briefly discusses key results. All results can be accessed on the ResStock Open Energy Data Initiative “End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock” data lake and on the data viewer at resstock.nlr.gov. Measure Summary Measure Title Advanced Air Sealing, Attic Floor Insulation, and Duct Sealing Measure This upgrade measure package applies advanced air sealing, attic floor insulation, Definition and duct sealing and insulation for applicable dwelling units. A dwelling unit may receive none, some, or all three individual measures, depending on its housing characteristics. Applicability This measure applies to all dwellings that have one of the following housing characteristics: • Equal or more than 6 ACH50 infiltration rate • Unfinished attic & less than R-49 attic floor insulation & in climate zone 1 • Unfinished attic & less than R-60 attic floor insulation & in climate zones 2 through 8 • More than 6% duct leakage to outside • Less than R-6 duct insulation. With these applicability constraints, 97.9% of the existing dwelling units receive at least one of the measures. Not Applicable This measure does not apply to dwelling units that have none of the following housing characteristics: • Equal or more than 6 ACH50 infiltration rate • Unfinished attic & less than R-49 attic floor insulation & in climate zone 1 • Unfinished attic & less than R-60 attic floor insulation & in climate zones 2 through 8 • More than 6% duct leakage to outside • Less than R-6 duct insulation. These constraints exclude 2.1% of the dwelling units from receiving this measure upgrade. File(s) 1 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 1 Technology Summary This upgrade package, which includes advanced air sealing, attic floor insulation, and duct sealing, combines three key areas of a retrofit measures. The goal of these upgrades is to reduce heat losses in winter and retain cool air in the conditioned space during summer. Air sealing alone does not eliminate the need for insulation (DOE, 2025). Insulation and air sealing work best together to improve comfort and energy efficiency. Therefore, they are often implemented as a package to address complementary aspects of a home’s energy performance, and their combined effect is much greater than any single measure alone. Together, these upgrades help to lower energy bills, enhance indoor comfort and improve indoor air quality year round. 1.1 Introduction to Technology Air Sealing Air sealing involves identifying and closing large and small gaps, cracks, and penetrations in the home’s primary or secondary pressure boundaries, such as around windows, doors, attic hatches, and plumbing or wiring holes (DOE, 2025). These leaks, whether large or small, accumulate and can allow a substantial amount of heated or cooled air escape.
